title: 5.10.5 Lab: Shoot them down
description: Shots fly straight through the enemies. Write hitEnemies: every shot against every enemy, a hit that removes the shot and takes 1 hp, and an enemy at 0 hp that scores its worth and leaves all three arrays.

steps.title: Every shot against every enemy
steps.instructions: Shots fly through enemies because nothing tests them. All your work is in `hitEnemies()`, which `draw()` already calls. Write a loop over `bullets` from the end to the start, and inside it a loop over `enemies` from the end to the start, as 5.10.4 showed. When `bullets[i]` overlaps `enemies[j]`, delete the shot, splice it out of `bullets`, and `break`: that shot is gone, so it must not be tested against the other enemies. Run it: a shot that reaches an enemy should vanish.
hints: Two backwards loops, one inside the other: `for (let i = bullets.length - 1; i >= 0; i--)` outside, and the same shape with `j` and `enemies` inside.
`break` goes last inside the overlap `if`, after everything the hit does.

steps.title: A hit takes 1 hp
steps.instructions: On the same hit, take 1 from `enemyHp[j]` and show the new number on the enemy with `enemies[j].text = String(enemyHp[j]);`. Run it: an orange enemy's 3 should count down to 2, then 1.
hints: `enemyHp[j] -= 1;` changes the number; the `.text` line is what makes the change show.
Both lines go inside the overlap `if`, before the `break`.

steps.title: Shot down
steps.instructions: If that hit leaves `enemyHp[j]` at 0 or less, the enemy is shot down: add `enemyWorth[j]` to `score`, delete the enemy's sprite and splice index `j` out of all three arrays. A crimson enemy should score 10 and an orange one 30. These are the same four removal lines as the landing in `moveEnemies()`; if you would rather type them once, move them into `function removeEnemy(j)` and call it from both places (the check reads it too).
hints: Add `enemyWorth[j]` to `score` before the splices: once index `j` is spliced, `enemyWorth[j]` belongs to a different enemy.
`if (enemyHp[j] <= 0) { ... }` holds the score line and the four removal lines.

requirements.title: Every shot is tested against every enemy
requirements.description: hitEnemies has a loop over bullets and, inside it, a loop over enemies (either way round), and tests them with overlaps. Help: 5.10.4 (Reading: Every shot against every enemy)

requirements.title: A hit removes the shot
requirements.description: The shot that hit is deleted from the screen and spliced out of bullets. Help: 5.10.4 (Reading: Every shot against every enemy)

requirements.title: A hit takes 1 hp
requirements.description: On a hit, enemyHp[j] goes down by 1. Help: 5.10.4 (Reading: Every shot against every enemy)

requirements.title: At 0 hp the enemy scores its worth and leaves all three arrays
requirements.description: When enemyHp[j] reaches 0, score goes up by enemyWorth[j] and index j is spliced out of enemies, enemyHp and enemyWorth (in hitEnemies, or in a removeEnemy helper it calls). Help: 5.10.4 (Reading: Every shot against every enemy)

requirements.title: A shot that hit is not tested again
requirements.description: After a hit the inner loop stops with break (or return), so a shot that has been spliced out is never read again. Help: 2.4.27 (Worked Example: break Leaves Only the Inner Loop)
